NONE: › to use chemicals to prevent a dead body from decaying
（用藥物等）對（屍體）進行防腐處理
› an artificial slope made of earth and/or stones
堤，堤岸，堤圍；（路）堤

example: a river/road/railway embankment
河堤／路堤／鐵路路堤

NONE: › an order to temporarily stop something, especially trading or giving information
（尤指暫時禁止貿易或提供消息的）禁令，禁運；限制
› to officially stop trading with another country
禁止與（另一國家）通商；對…禁運

example: They have put an embargo on imports of clothing.
他們已經禁止進口服裝。
The police asked for a news embargo while they tried to find the kidnapper.
警方要求在他們搜捕綁架者期間，停止相關的新聞報道。
They are planning to embargo oil imports.
他們正在計劃禁止石油進口。

NONE: › to go onto a ship
上船

example: We embarked at Liverpool for New York.
我們從利物浦登船，前往紐約。
Opposite
disembark

NONE: › to start something new or important
開始，著手做（新的或重要的事情）

example: We're embarking upon a new project later this year.
今年晚些時候我們會著手進行一個新企劃。

NONE: C2 to cause someone to feel nervous, worried, or uncomfortable
使尷尬，使窘迫；使爲難

example: You're embarrassing him with your compliments!
你的讚美之詞使他很不好意思。
I didn't want to embarrass her in front of her friends.
我並不想在她朋友面前讓她感到難堪。

NONE: B1 feeling ashamed or shy
窘迫的，尷尬的；害羞的
› having no money
拮据的

example: She felt embarrassed about undressing in front of the doctor.
在醫生面前脫衣服讓她覺得很尷尬。
[ + to infinitive ] I was too embarrassed to admit that I was scared.
我不好意思承認我被嚇壞了。

NONE: B1 making you feel embarrassed
使人感到窘迫的，令人尷尬的，使人難堪的

example: an embarrassing situation
令人尷尬的情形
[ + to infinitive ] It's embarrassing to be caught telling a lie.
說謊被人當場識破是件很尷尬的事情。
My most embarrassing moment was trying to introduce a woman whose name I couldn't remember.
我最狼狽的一刻是，我想要介紹一位女士卻怎麽也想不起來她的名字。

NONE: B2 the feeling of being embarrassed, or something that makes you feel embarrassed
尷尬，窘迫；侷促不安；令人尷尬的事

example: She blushed with embarrassment.
她難堪得臉都紅了。
My parents are an embarrassment to me!
我父母讓我覺得很丟臉！

NONE: B1 the group of people who represent their country in a foreign country
大使館全體人員，使館館員
B1 the building that these people work in
大使館

example: We used to be friendly with some people who worked at the Swedish Embassy.
我們曾經和瑞典大使館的一些工作人員關係非常友好。
The Ambassador held a reception at the embassy.
大使在大使館舉行了招待會。

NONE: › having a lot of problems or difficulties
危機四伏的；處境艱難的

example: an embattled government
危機四伏的政府

NONE: › to fix something firmly into a substance
把…牢牢嵌入（或插入、埋入）
› fixed into the surface of something
嵌入（或插入、埋入）…之中的
› If an emotion, opinion, etc. is embedded in someone or something, it is a very strong or important part of him, her, or it.
（感情、態度等）深切的；根深蒂固的；強烈感受到的
› An embedded journalist or reporter travels with and is protected by a unit of soldiers during a war.
（記者）隨軍採訪的

example: The thorn was embedded in her thumb.
刺紮進了她的大拇指。
A sense of guilt was deeply embedded in my conscience.
一種罪惡感在我內心打下了深深的烙印。

NONE: › a computer system that does a particular task inside a machine or larger electrical system
（電腦）嵌入式系統

example: Vending machines, turnstiles and meters will come with embedded systems that will communicate with big computers over the web.
自動販賣機、驗票閘門和汽車停放計時器都裝有嵌入式系統，通過網路跟大型電腦交流。

NONE: › to make something more beautiful or interesting by adding something to it
裝飾，修飾；給…錦上添花，渲染

example: The ceiling was embellished with flowers and leaves.
天花板上裝飾著花和葉。
He couldn't resist embellishing the story of his accident a little.
在描述他出的那次意外時，他忍不住添油加醋地渲染了一番。

NONE: › a piece of wood or coal, etc. that continues to burn after a fire has no more flames
餘燄未盡的木塊（或煤塊）

example: We sat by the glowing/dying embers of the fire.
我們坐在餘燄未盡／將盡的爐火旁。

NONE: › to secretly take money that is in your care or that belongs to an organization or business you work for
貪汙，侵吞；盜用，挪用（錢款）

example: She embezzled thousands of dollars from the charity.
她侵吞了慈善機構數千美元的善款。

NONE: › very angry about unfair things that have happened to you
怨憤的，怨恨的

example: They ignored all her pleas and she became very embittered.
他們對她的所有懇求都置之不理，她因此忿忿不平。
He died a disillusioned and embittered old man.
年邁遲暮的他萬念俱灰，飲恨而終。

NONE: › to print or decorate something in a very noticeable way
（醒目地）印製，裝飾；炫示

example: Her name was emblazoned across the front of the theatre.
她的名字赫然印在劇院正面的牆上。
cars emblazoned with the company logo
醒目地裝飾著公司標誌的汽車

NONE: › a picture of an object that is used to represent a particular person, group, or idea
象徵；標誌；符號；徽章

example: A rose is the national emblem of England.
玫瑰是英國的標誌。

NONE: › representing a particular person, group, or idea
象徵的；可當標誌的

example: A sword is emblematic of power gained by violence.
劍象徵著藉由暴力獲取的權力。

NONE: › someone or something that represents a quality or an idea exactly
（某種品質或思想的）化身，表現；典型

example: He was the embodiment of the English gentleman.
他是典型的英國紳士。
She was portrayed in the papers as the embodiment of evil.
她被報紙描述爲邪惡的化身。

NONE: C2 to represent a quality or an idea exactly
具體表現；體現
› to include as part of something
包括，包含；收錄

example: She embodied good sportsmanship on the playing field.
在運動場上，她展現了優秀的體育精神。
Kennett embodied in one man an unusual range of science, music, and religion.
肯尼特集科學、音樂、宗教等方面一系列非凡成就於一身。

NONE: › to make someone brave
使有膽量

example: Emboldened by drink, he walked over to speak to her.
他借酒壯膽，走上前去與她搭訕。

NONE: › a bubble of air, a mass of blood that has become hard, or a small piece of fat that blocks an artery
（血管的）栓塞，血栓
› the action of deliberately blocking the flow of blood in a particular blood vessel by putting material into the blood
栓塞術；栓塞形成

example: Unlike hysterectomies, uterine artery embolization is not 100 percent effective for treating fibroids.
與子宮切除術不同，子宮動脈栓塞對治療類纖維瘤並不是百分之百有效。

NONE: › to decorate an object, especially with letters, using special tools that make a raised mark on its surface
在…表面上用浮雕圖案裝飾；（尤指）在…上壓印浮凸字體

example: She handed me a business card with her name neatly embossed on it.
她遞給我一張名片，上面簡潔地凸印著她的名字。

T: C1 [ T ] formal to accept something enthusiastically

I or T: C2 [ I or T ] literary to hold someone tightly with both arms to express love, liking, or sympathy, or when greeting or leaving someone

T: C1 [ T ] formal to include something, often as one of a number of things

NONE: C2 the act of holding someone tightly with both arms to express love, liking, or sympathy, or when greeting or leaving someone
抱，擁抱

example: This was an opportunity that he would embrace.
這樣的機會他是求之不得的。
She saw them embrace on the station platform.
她看到他們在月臺上擁抱。
He leaned over to embrace the child.
他彎腰去擁抱那個孩子。
Linguistics embraces a diverse range of subjects such as phonetics and stylistics.
語言學包括一系列不同的科目，如語音學和文體學。
She greeted me with a warm embrace.
她用熱烈的擁抱迎接我。

NONE: › a liquid that is rubbed onto the body to reduce pain or stiffness in muscles
（用於緩解肌肉疼痛或僵硬的）擦劑

I or T: › to decorate cloth or clothing with patterns or pictures consisting of stitches that are sewn directly onto the material
› to make a story more entertaining by adding imaginary details to it

example: I am embroidering this picture for my mother.
我正在爲媽媽繡這幅畫。
Naturally, I embroidered the tale a little to make it more interesting.
很自然地，我講這個故事時作了一點渲染，好讓它更有趣。

C or U: › [ C or U ] patterns or pictures that consist of stitches sewn directly onto cloth
U: › [ U ] the activity of decorating a piece of cloth with stitches sewn onto it
› [ U ] the way that someone makes a story more entertaining by adding imaginary details to it

example: Let me show you Pat's embroideries.
我給你看看派特的刺繡作品。
It was a beautiful piece of embroidery.
這是一件漂亮的刺繡作品。
I'm not very good at embroidery.
我不擅長刺繡。
comic embroidery
喜劇渲染

NONE: › to cause someone to become involved in an argument or a difficult situation
使捲入（糾紛）；使陷入（困境）

example: She had no desire to embroil herself in lengthy lawsuits with the tabloid newspapers.
她不想捲入和那些小報的漫長官司糾紛中。
The United Nations was reluctant to get its forces embroiled in civil war.
聯合國不願讓其維和部隊捲入國家的內戰中。

NONE: › an animal that is developing either in its mother's womb or in an egg, or a plant that is developing in a seed
胚，胚胎
› developing and not yet complete
在胚胎階段，在萌芽階段；尚未成熟

example: Between the eighth week of development and birth a human embryo is called a foetus.
從發育第八周到出生這段時間，人類的胚胎被稱作胎兒。
The department's plans for enlargement are still in embryo.
這個系的擴建計劃仍在醞釀之中。

NONE: › the study of animal development between the fertilization of the egg and the time when the animal is born
胚胎學
› relating to an embryo
胚的，胚胎的

before noun: › [ before noun ] formal starting to develop
萌芽期的；剛起步的；未成熟的

example: The project is still at an embryonic stage.
這個專案仍處於剛起步階段。
